all_found.desc: [BUG] Checkpoint skips non-passing markers individually, so a PASS at C3 superseded by a later NEEDS_REVISION at the same head is still the checkpoint; the gate's own rule is last-recorded-wins. Reproduced: PASS@c2 then NEEDS_REVISION@c2 then commit c3 -> checkpoint c2; the next increment treats rejected code as reviewed.

[BUG] Checkpoint trusts any passing lens marker without requiring its base..head to chain back to the fork point, and pr-ready's projector derives ChangedPaths from checkpoint..HEAD only, so blockers on files changed before the checkpoint become 'unrelated'. Reproduced: a task-done NEEDS_REVISION blocker on a.go (changed before the checkpoint) is dropped and `review pr-ready --base last-reviewed` exits 0 PASS_ADVISORY while --base main is NEEDS_REVISION.

[ADVISORY] An incremental PASS carries no trace that it reviewed only checkpoint..HEAD (records store the SHA, not the token); docs still describe pr-ready as whole-branch. A pr-ready PASS log can be read as whole-branch evidence.
[ADVISORY] resolveBaseToken was inserted between refuseFlagShapedTarget's doc comment and its func, misattributing both godocs. Misleading documentation; linters flag it.

[ADVISORY] After merging main into the branch the checkpoint is the pre-merge head, so checkpoint..HEAD includes upstream changes brought in by the merge. The incremental review re-reviews main's commits (verified); on a busy main it balloons.

[BUG] Any isAncestor error aborts resolution; `merge-base --is-ancestor` exits 128 when a marker's head no longer exists locally (rebased/amended head pruned by gc, or runs.jsonl copied to another clone). After a routine rebase + gc, --base last-reviewed and review checkpoint fail hard on a stale marker instead of skipping it.

[ADVISORY] The strict-ancestor skip (m.HeadSHA == head) and the record-lenses wiring survive mutation: the fake isAncestor is non-reflexive and no CLI test records a marker at HEAD or uses record-lenses --base last-reviewed. The central strict-ancestor rule is untested.

[BUG] The checkpoint's fork point and pr-ready's whole-branch blocker scope come from gitcontext.DefaultBase, which falls back to HEAD~1 with no local main/master (develop/trunk repos, CI checkouts). Reproduced in a develop-trunk repo: incremental pr-ready passes (exit 0) with an open task-done blocker on a file changed before the checkpoint; a narrow-base marker becomes the checkpoint.

[ADVISORY] Fork-point wiring is untested against real git: DefaultBase->HEAD~1 and forkPoint := head mutants survive; no CLI test refuses a narrow-base marker. A fork-point regression would accept narrow-base checkpoints silently.

[ADVISORY] The exit-2 message and commands/skills docs say 'no passing review recorded' / 'with none recorded', but since 7ac29ab it also exits 2 when passing reviews exist but none qualifies (superseded, narrow base, no base, rebased chain); commands/review-pr-ready.md lacks the whole-branch-blockers sentence. Users who just recorded a narrow-base review are told none exists.

[BUG] defaultBase reports forked=true with base==HEAD whenever merge-base(HEAD, main)==HEAD and the branch is not named main (detached HEAD at main's tip, or a branch fast-forwarded into local main). ForkPoint passes it through, so Checkpoint's isAncestor(base, forkPoint=HEAD) is true for any marker base. Reproduced: on main a PASS marker over C2..C3, commit C4; checkpoint exits 2 on main but returns C3 after `git checkout --detach` though fork..C2 was never reviewed; incremental pr-ready scopes whole-branch blockers to an empty HEAD..HEAD diff.

findings.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The no-fork-point exit-2 message says 'no local main or master it branched from', which is wrong since 358237a when main exists and HEAD is merely reachable from it (detached main tip, branch fast-forwarded into main, branch with no commits of its own). A user on a detached main tip is told main doesn't exist and looks for the wrong cause.

rejected.desc: [BUG] Only a later marker at the same head withdraws a checkpoint; a later NEEDS_REVISION at a descendant head whose base is at/before the checkpoint also judged the checkpoint's code but is ignored. Reproduced: PASS@C1 (base main), NEEDS_REVISION@C2 (base main), C3 -> checkpoint C1, incremental pr-ready C1..C3 passes, hiding the rejection.

[ADVISORY] The cycle guard is untested; the only real cycle is a base==head marker (record-lenses --base HEAD), where vouches(h) recurses into itself. Removing the guard makes checkpoint resolution overflow the stack on such a marker with the suite green.

[ADVISORY] The CLI Incremental wiring for task-done and epic-ready is untested (deleting either survives). Incremental task-done/epic-ready runs could silently record the SHA instead of last-reviewed.
